title: Rational peptide design for inhibition of the KIX-MLL interaction.
authors: Sato, Nao; Suetaka, Shunji; Hayashi, Yuuki; Arai, Munehito
one_liner_zh: 该文用Rosetta设计抑制KIX-MLL互作的肽段，涉及转录共激活因子与转录激活因子的蛋白-蛋白互作，但非TF-DNA结合体系，且方法为蛋白设计而非AI/物理模拟，仅部分相关。
abstract: The kinase-inducible domain interacting (KIX) domain is an integral part of the general transcriptional coactivator CREB-binding protein, and has been associated with leukemia, cancer, and various viral diseases. Hence, the KIX domain has attracted considerable attention in drug discovery and development. Here, we rationally designed a KIX inhibitor using a peptide fragment corresponding to the transactivation domain (TAD) of the transcriptional activator, mixed-lineage leukemia protein (MLL). We performed theoretical saturation mutagenesis using the Rosetta software to search for mutants expected to bind KIX more tightly than the wild-type MLL TAD. Mutant peptides with higher helical propensities were selected for experimental characterization. We found that the T2857W mutant of the MLL TAD peptide had the highest binding affinity for KIX compared to the other 12 peptides designed in this study. Moreover, the peptide had a high inhibitory effect on the KIX-MLL interaction with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration close to the dissociation constant for this interaction. To our knowledge, this peptide has the highest affinity for KIX among all previously reported inhibitors that target the MLL site of KIX. Thus, our approach may be useful for rationally developing helical peptides that inhibit protein-protein interactions implicated in the progression of various diseases.
abstract_zh: 激酶诱导结构域相互作用（KIX）结构域是通用转录共激活因子CREB结合蛋白的组成部分，并与白血病、癌症及多种病毒性疾病相关。因此，KIX结构域在药物发现与开发中引起了广泛关注。在此，我们基于转录激活因子混合谱系白血病蛋白（MLL）的反式激活结构域（TAD）对应的肽段片段，合理设计了一种KIX抑制剂。我们利用Rosetta软件进行了理论饱和突变，以寻找预期比野生型MLL TAD更紧密结合KIX的突变体。选择了具有更高螺旋倾向性的突变肽进行实验表征。我们发现，在本研究设计的其他12种肽中，MLL TAD肽的T2857W突变体对KIX具有最高的结合亲和力。此外，该肽对KIX-MLL相互作用具有高抑制效果，其半数抑制浓度接近该相互作用的解离常数。据我们所知，在所有先前报道的靶向KIX MLL位点的抑制剂中，该肽对KIX具有最高的亲和力。因此，我们的方法可能有助于合理开发抑制多种疾病进展中涉及的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用的螺旋肽。
